sources.note: The language is not in the catalog and has no existing statements; Campbell 2024 adds no phonological information. It confirms independently what Rowe 1950, Loukotka 1968 and Adelaar & Muysken 2004 already say: the corpus is one common noun (tubete) plus one name (Hijuoba), so no word-stress statement is possible.

sources.citation: d'Olwer, Luis Nicolau (ed.). 1963 [reimpr. 2012]. Cronistas de las culturas precolombinas: antología. México: Fondo de Cultura Económica (Biblioteca Americana). Section 'Fray Matías de San Francisco', pp. 421-424, incl. '[De los indios idibais o de la Gorgona]' = Relación de los indios idibais, 1636, reprinted from Córdoba Salinas, Crónica, lib. I, cap. XXX.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology. The only linguistic remark is the 1636 sentence already held by the project from Córdoba Salinas 1651/1957: 'Es su lengua más fácil que otras, por finalizar siempre en vocales' (words always end in a vowel). Adds alternative ethnonym spellings idibáis, iribis, ibidáis. Nothing on stress, accent or tone; no word forms beyond those already known.
